origin: cwe/416/cpp Key Principles: use std::weak_ptr for an observer that may outlive the object, and lock() at the point of use

finding.name: Use After Free
finding.summary: EventBus stores raw Observer pointers with no unsubscribe path. monitorOnce() subscribes a stack-local SensorObserver and returns, destroying it while EventBus still holds the pointer; the next publish() dereferences the dangling pointer.

trap: Adding a destructor to SensorObserver that calls an unsubscribe method on the bus only fixes observers that are destroyed through their own destructor and that remember which bus they registered with; it does not change what EventBus itself stores, so any other observer lifetime path (a moved-from observer, a container that erases without running destructors, a bus outliving process shutdown order) reproduces the same dangling pointer. The durable fix is for EventBus to store std::weak_ptr<Observer> and require observers to be held via shared_ptr, so publish() can skip an expired observer instead of dereferencing a stale raw pointer.
must_preserve: publish() still calls onEvent() on every currently-subscribed, live observer, in subscription order. An observer that is properly unsubscribed before publish() runs must not be invoked.
